questions.q: What are the three groups of objects in Tableau's Analytics pane?
options: Sort, Group, and Bin
Summarize, Model, and Custom
Filters, Marks, and Shelves
Dimensions, Measures, and Sets
questions.explain: Summarize describes data you already have (averages, medians), Model fits something to it (trend, forecast, cluster), and Custom lets you draw a fixed line or band yourself.

questions.q: What does a trend line actually do?
options: Removes outliers from the underlying data source
Fits a line (linear by default) through historical data to show the general direction — it does not predict future values on its own
Converts a dimension into a measure
Automatically predicts sales for the next 12 months
questions.explain: A trend line fits the historical pattern already in the data — projecting into the future is what Forecasting does, a separate Analytics pane object.

questions.q: Why does a forecast's confidence band typically widen the further it projects into the future?
options: The band width is fixed and never actually changes
It's a rendering bug that has no real meaning
It indicates the forecast has failed and should be ignored entirely
Tableau is being honest that a projection further from the last real data point is less certain than one closer to it
questions.explain: The widening shaded band reflects genuinely increasing uncertainty the further out the forecast extends — a forecast whose band doesn't widen should be treated with suspicion.

questions.q: How does a Reference Line differ from a Trend Line?
options: A Reference Line draws a single fixed, user-specified value; a Trend Line is fitted to the actual data
They are functionally identical with different names
Reference Lines can only be used with dates, never with numbers
A Reference Line is fitted to the data; a Trend Line is a fixed user-specified value
questions.explain: A Reference Line marks a number you specify directly (a goal or target) — unlike a Trend Line, it doesn't fit anything to the underlying data.

questions.q: What does right-clicking a trend line and choosing 'Describe Trend Model' show you?
options: A list of every dashboard the trend line has ever appeared on
The exact pixel coordinates of the line on screen
The line's actual statistical fit, including its R² value and statistical significance
An option to convert the trend line into a forecast automatically
questions.explain: Describe Trend Model reveals the real statistics behind the fitted line — R² and significance — instead of just eyeballing how well it seems to fit.
